summary: Not ready for 'done'. The list misses or wrongly excludes plants a Valmont-focused sales team will know: Valmont Valley NE (excluded as an irrigation campus although a posting at 28800 Ida St says it welds poles with MIG and flux-core) and Valmont El Dorado KS (not in the ledger; posting dated Oct 2026 for 'fabrication of steel electrical poles'). V&S Schuler (Canton OH, Muskogee OK, Burton OH) and ROHN Peoria IL are also absent. El Dorado, V&S and ROHN are in the repo's own AISC snapshot and in neither auditor's list; Valley was listed by both auditors and still left excluded. Three profiled plants, including the High-scoring Meyer Tulsa, have never been fact-checked, yet the run log and map say every profiled plant has been. The 5/64 = 7.8% miss rate reproduces but is a lower bound: the auditors share the finder's blind spots and the denominator rule is inconsistent (variants 9.6% and 10.6%); against the plants now verified, the first-pass miss was at least 12/71 = 16.9% and at least 5/71 = 7.0% is still outstanding. Fact error rates recompute (11.8%; 19.4% as reported or 17.9% on the row unit the other rounds use; 8.2%; pooled 11.3%). Of the 31 exclusions, 5 are disputed, 18 accepted and 8 depend on a boundary rule that is not written down. Other fixes: Elkhart and Plymouth exclusions are inconsistent with FWT's inclusion, MICA Kaufman's record contradicts itself, and one link has an unreachable source. Not verified by me: posting open status for Valley, V&S Burton's product, ROHN's in-house welding, a row-by-row diff of the 252 AISC Highway Component Manufacturer holders, the 26 exclusions I accepted from the ledger's own evidence, and the leads in coverage-5.

findings.finding: Valmont's Valley, NE plant is excluded as an 'irrigation plant campus' with 'no source found that names poles made there'. Sources below show it welds steel poles (and Valmont is a reported Path customer, so this is a customer_other_plant). Its products row ('Irrigation equipment', tagged stated) rests on a 10-K sentence about the Agriculture segment that does not name Valley's products. Both list auditors rated Valley in definition (B: high) with quoted DOT sources, and the coordinator still counted it as 'found' without revisiting the exclusion.

Posting date/open status not read; confirm before using for labor points. (2) https://www.mass.gov/info-details/approved-fabricators-of-signs-luminaires-and-signal-supports (--check FOUND): "Valmont Industries – Valley, NE" under "approved to manufacture overhead and cantilever sign supports, highway and high mast lighting supports, strain poles, and traffic signal supports". (4) Auditor A row: roads.maryland.gov/OMT/lightstruc.pdf "Valley NE (SM8) 28800 Ida Street"; auditor B row: GDOT qpl52a.pdf "Valmont Industries, Inc. – Valley, NE". findings.fix: plants.csv p-valmont-valley-ne: status excluded -> base, clear exclusion_reason, name -> 'Valmont - Valley (steel poles; also irrigation campus)', products -> steel poles (lighting, traffic, sign and high-mast supports per DOT lists), relationship customer_other_plant. Then send to a plant-profiler (weld_processes MIG/FCAW is stated in source 1) and a fact-checker. It will likely score Medium or High.

findings.finding: The reported miss rate (5/64 = 7.8%) reproduces arithmetically, but it is not a sound estimate of list completeness and should not be read as 'the list is 92% complete'. (1) The denominator is inconsistent: Elkhart and Ferndale were removed from numerator and denominator as 'unverified', while 12 auditor rows that the ledger itself excludes as unverified or out of definition stay in the denominator as 'found' (Valley, Plymouth, Commercial Fabricators, Clarkson, Leitchfield, Interstate Structures, Steve Johnson, Hadco, Griffin, Greenacres, Flagpoles Inc, TAPP, which has no US plant). (2) Elkhart and Ferndale were real finder misses at audit time; removing them after the fact lowers the rate by redefining the test. (3) The two auditors are same-method agents that share the finder's blind spots: every plant in findings 2-4 is absent from both auditor lists, so the audit cannot detect that class of miss. (4) ledger/audit/miss-candidates-v-poles-substation.json is stale (81 in definition, 76 matched, 5 unmatched; still maps 'Meyer Utility Structures - Tulsa', 'Arcosa Telecom Structures - Tulsa' and 'Lyte Poles' to other plants by city) and does not reproduce any reported figure; the map embeds it. (5) verticals.csv reason still says 'Plant list complete (94 found, 60 included ... miss rate 6.3%)'.
findings.evidence: Recount from the two auditor files: 107 in-definition rows = 68 unique plants. Minus DIS-TRAN Chicago Heights (out of definition), Elkhart, Ferndale and Arcosa Telecom Tulsa (not distinct) = 64; misses Birmingham, Raycap, Brookshire, Cem-Tec, Meyer Tulsa = 5/64 = 7.8% (matches the log). Alternatives: as-audited rule (Elkhart and Ferndale counted as misses) 7/66 = 10.6%; consistent 'ledger-verified in-definition only' rule (drop the 12 excluded rows too) 5/52 = 9.6%. Independent estimate from this review: verified in-definition plants now known = 66 profiled + Valley + El Dorado + V&S Canton + V&S Muskogee + ROHN Peoria = 71; the plant-finder slices originally found 59 of them (66 minus the 4 auditor misses, Meyer Tulsa, HW Metals and Ameron 66th St), so first-pass miss was at least 12/71 = 16.9%, and at least 5/71 = 7.0% is still missing or wrongly excluded today (7/73 = 9.6% if V&S Burton and CommStructures confirm). The 7.0% floor leaves out Elkhart, Plymouth, Salem and Flagpoles Inc, which coverage-8 and coverage-10 recommend reinstating; with those four the outstanding figure would be 9/75 = 12.0%. My pass was not exhaustive (about 25 searches; the 252 Highway Component Manufacturer holders in the AISC snapshot were scanned by name, not diffed row by row), so these are floors. If the coverage-5 leads confirm, the first-pass miss passes CLAUDE.md's 20% line, which requires an advisor checkpoint.
findings.fix: In run_log.md and on the map Method page: (a) state the miss rate as '5/64 = 7.8% against two auditors who share the finder's sources; a reviewer pass found at least 5 further plants (list them), so treat 7.8% as a lower bound'; (b) show the 10.6% and 9.6% variants with their rules; (c) regenerate miss-candidates-v-poles-substation.json with the company-name matcher fix or stop embedding it; (d) replace the verticals.csv reason text ('Plant list complete ... 6.3%') with current counts; (e) log an advisor consultation if the recomputed first-pass miss rate is over 20% once the coverage-5 leads are resolved; (f) for the next vertical give one auditor a seeded-recall test (hold back 5 known plants and check the finder returns them) and require the auditors to name-scan the AISC snapshot.

findings.finding: The 'current operation unverified' bar is applied unevenly inside the same parent tier. Valmont Elkhart is excluded for lack of a current pole source, yet the AISC snapshot taken on 2026-11-12 lists it as a currently certified Highway Component Manufacturer, Ohio DOT lists it for signal supports and strain poles, and the log admits 2026 steel-welder postings were seen in snippets. Valmont Plymouth is excluded because 'pole or monopole production not stated on the locations page', but it is on the MassDOT approved list for sign, luminaire and signal supports (auditors A and B both quoted this; B also cites a WisDOT sign-structure listing at 1545 Pidco Dr). The run log itself (fact-check round 1 entry, line 160) records 'a 2017 communication-structures brochure that places production at Plymouth IN and Salem OR', which contradicts both exclusion reasons ('in-scope pole or monopole production not stated on the locations page') for p-valmont-plymouth-in and p-valmont-salem-or. Meanwhile FWT Fort Worth and FWT Hicksville are profiled on a single 2015 company-level sentence with every profile field unknown.
findings.evidence: AISC snapshot: "Valmont Industries, Inc. - Elkhart	Elkhart	IN	Highway Component Manufacturer" and "Valmont Industries, Inc. - Plymouth	Plymouth	IN	Bridge Fabricator - Simple". Mass.gov page fetched 2026-11-13 lists "Valmont Industries - Plymouth, IN" under fabricators "approved to manufacture overhead and cantilever sign supports, highway and high mast lighting supports, strain poles, and traffic signal supports". evidence.csv p-valmont-elkhart-in:products (stated, confirmed) "Signal Supports and Strain Poles Certified"; p-fwt-fort-worth-tx:products (inferred) quotes only the 2015 wirelessestimator.com article; p-fwt-*:weld_processes and :welder_postings = unknown. Search results in this review show Sabre welder postings for Hicksville OH (app.energyhire.com, 2025), which would give FWT Hicksville a current source.
findings.fix: One rule for all four: a plant with a current government or certification listing for an in-scope product is 'base' (included, low confidence), not excluded. Apply: p-valmont-elkhart-in -> base with the AISC row added as evidence and a research task to fetch a 2026 posting; p-valmont-plymouth-in -> base with the Mass.gov row as products evidence ('sign, luminaire and signal supports; telecom towers'), flagged for a profiler to separate welded pole/sign work from bolted towers. p-valmont-salem-or: have a plant-finder read the 2017 brochure and a current source for monopole or welded-section production at Salem; base if a source places it there, else keep excluded with the brochure cited in the reason. For FWT Fort Worth and Hicksville, fetch a current Sabre posting or site page per plant; if none is found for Fort Worth, apply the Ferndale rule and exclude it.

findings.area: definition boundary: sign shops, contract fabricators, towers
findings.finding: Three boundary rules are applied case by case rather than by a written test. (1) DOT-list-only fabricators: Larwel, QMF, Metal Pros and PennFab are profiled as contract fabricators on the strength of a state approved-fabricator listing for sign structures, while Ackerman & Baynes, L&M Fabrication, Griffin Welding, Specialty Fab and Commercial Fabricators are excluded although they sit on equivalent lists (MassDOT, WisDOT, AISC HCM). The definition's exclusion of 'general fabricators that build such structures only as occasional custom jobs' needs an operational test. (2) LaX Spring Grove and Westby are in the vertical on one company-level sentence ('electrical substations columns, beams, and awnings'), tagged inferred for both plants; which plant makes substation steel is unknown. (3) Telecom towers: the definition excludes 'bolted lattice towers', but PiRod (Plymouth) and ROHN build welded tower sections as well as monopoles, and Sabre Sioux City and Nello South Bend are included with tower/pole mix unresolved; Plymouth and Salem are excluded on the same facts.
findings.evidence: plants.csv exclusion_reason text for the listed ids; evidence p-nello-spring-grove-mn:products and p-nello-westby-wi:products both quote https://nelloinc.com/our-divisions "LaX Industries manufactures a variety of structural steel products including electrical substations columns, beams, and awnings." (inferred). Mass.gov list (fetched) includes Griffin Welding, L&M Fabrication, Specialty Fab alongside profiled Metal Pros, Stony Brook and Hurtt.
findings.fix: Write the test into run_log.md and re-apply it to all DOT-list rows, e.g.: include when (a) the company's own page names the structure type as a product line, or (b) two or more current state approved-fabricator lists name the plant for it; otherwise exclude with 'occasional/unverified'. For towers: include a tower plant when a source states monopoles or welded tower sections are made there, and note 'tower/pole mix unknown'. findings.finding: The three reported rates recompute, with two caveats on honesty of presentation. Round 1: 42 corrected / 355 checked (136 + 88 + 131, 1 unreachable excluded) = 11.8%, correct. Round 2: reported 12/62 = 19.4%; file B holds 45 verdict rows for 40 claim_ids (5 claims have two source rows), while every other file counts verdict rows (files 1-3 and round 3 also contain repeated claim_ids and count each row); on the same unit round 2 is 12/67 = 17.9%. Round 3: 18/219 = 8.2%, correct, but checker C alone found 10/55 = 18.2% and the round excludes the three plants in coverage-6. Pooled over all rounds the rate is 72/636 = 11.3%. Round 3 was a census, not a sample: it covered 219 stated rows on 23 plants, and those plants carry 217 stated rows today. The 'under 10% -> done' rule is met only by this last round, which was measured after a clean-up that had already corrected 95 of 263 previously unchecked stated rows (36%) across the 60 plants then profiled. No post-correction re-measurement exists for the round 1 and round 2 plants.
